Article Title: Watch: Manoj Tiwari offers Usha Arghya in Delhi's Yamuna; BJP leaders join Chhath celebrations
Article Text:
Chhath celebrations in Delhi: Manoj Tiwari performs Usha Arghya rituals in Yamuna

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari on Monday performed the Usha Arghya rituals of Chhath Puja in Yamuna river in Delhi, accompanied by his wife, Surabhi Tiwari.The rituals coincided with the final day of the four-day festival, as devotees gathered along riverbanks and other water bodies across the country to offer prayers to the rising Sun.The North East Delhi MP, who hails from Purvanchal, participated in the rituals with his wife, who has been observing the festival for the third consecutive year.Speaking to news agency ANI after offering prayers, Tiwari said the banks of the Yamuna in Delhi were filled with devotees observing Chhath, with celebrations extending across a stretch of approximately 15 kilometres."The banks of the Yamuna in Delhi are filled with those observing Chhath—the celebrations extend for about 15 kilometres along this stretch. It is early morning, and the time has come to offer 'arghya' to the rising Sun God. Having already offered 'arghya' to the setting sun, we are now here at the ghat on the banks of the Yamuna in Delhi to offer it to the rising sun. There is such immense joy here--truly, a wonderful atmosphere," he said.Tiwari also said the scale of Chhath celebrations in Delhi had grown significantly, crediting the BJP-led government for making arrangements for devotees."The scale at which Chhath is being celebrated in Delhi right now is something the people here had never even imagined. At one point, Chhath celebrations on the Yamuna were even prohibited, but thanks to the government--the BJP government led by PM Modi--we have managed to put all the necessary arrangements in place," he said.Weeks earlier, the actor-turned-politician had taken a dip in the Yamuna, claiming that the river's pollution load had reduced by half over the past year due to cleaning works undertaken by the Rekha Gupta government. He had also asserted that people could once again celebrate Chhath Puja in the Yamuna, news agency PTI reported.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to devotees on the conclusion of the four-day festival, saying the occasion reflected a remarkable confluence of faith, discipline and spiritual practice."Today, the four-day ritual of the grand festival of Chhath concluded with the offering of prayers to the rising sun. This divine festival dedicated to nature witnessed a remarkable confluence of steadfast resolve and spiritual practice. I pray to Chhathi Maiya to bestow her blessings on all the devotees observing the fast, as well as on my family members across the country," PM Modi posted on X.BJP chief Nitin Nabin also performed the final rituals of Chhath Puja with his wife, Deepmala, offering 'arghya' to the rising Sun.Speaking to reporters, Nabin prayed for happiness and prosperity for people across the country."I pray for the people of Bihar and the entire nation; may there be happiness and prosperity in everyone’s life," Nabin said.Nabin also described the festival as a reflection of Bihar's cultural traditions and said its message of cleanliness, purity and discipline was reaching people across the world."It is only through their blessings that we have been able to successfully conclude this four-day festival -- a period marked by rigorous discipline and physical hardship. Furthermore, the message emanating from Bihar today -- a message of cleanliness, purity, sanctity, and discipline -- is reaching the entire nation and the world. Long live Chhath Mata; long live the culture of Bihar."Former Union minister and Sambalpur MP Dharmendra Pradhan also performed Chhath Puja and offered 'arghya' to the rising Sun on Monday.Pradhan extended greetings to devotees across the country, including those in Odisha, Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bengal. He said Chhath had grown into a festival of great significance and was now celebrated across the world.Speaking after offering prayers, Pradhan said devotees had the opportunity to offer 'arghya' to the setting Sun on Sunday and the rising Sun on Monday, describing it as a fortunate occasion.Chhath Puja is a four-day festival dedicated to the worship of the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya. On the third day, devotees gather at riverbanks and other water bodies to offer 'arghya' to the setting Sun, a ritual known as Sandhya Arghya.The festival concluded on the fourth day with Usha Arghya, when devotees offered prayers to the rising Sun at dawn.
Article Summary: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari performs Usha Arghya rituals in Yamuna river in Delhi. Rituals coincided with the final day of the four-day festival. Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to devotees on the conclusion of the festival.

Article Title: Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC
Article Text:
Representative image

Errors likely in weeding out dead, non-existent voters: EC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has assured Supreme Court that all attempts will be made to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls and no prosecution would be launched against people whose names were deleted from the post-SIR draft electoral rolls, for using Form 6 for restoration of their names in the voters' lists.EC's stand, spelt out in an affidavit filed Saturday, is in sync with the Oct 26 assurance given by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana while hearing petitions relating to alleged large-scale deletion of voters in Maharashtra and Delhi. The CJI-led bench had said, "No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voters' lists."Petitioners had highlighted voters' apprehension that they might be prosecuted for giving a false declaration in Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters, that they had never been registered as voters before.EC said, "No prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely on the ground that the applicant/elector was previously enrolled in the electoral roll(s) prior to the SIR and their names did not appear in the draft electoral rolls during the SIR."However, EC said those filling Form 6 to restore their names in the electoral rolls must ensure their names do not figure in the voters' lists in any other assembly or parliamentary constituency.Assuring the court that efforts have been intensified to register every eligible citizen as a voter, EC said, "A mechanism has also been directed to be put in place to ensure that no elector is deprived of the opportunity to get his/her name included in the final electoral roll, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed eligibility conditions, while taking due care to avoid duplication in enrolment."Accepting that there may have been errors in weeding out non-existent and dead voters from the electoral rolls through SIR, the commission said, "There are challenges on count of the large numbers involved, and also because the full data is being digitised. There have been and will be problems that arise from time to time and the commission remains alive to the need to ensure that all those who are eligible to vote find their name in the voters' lists but equally, to ensure that all inconsistencies in these lists are addressed. "On complaints about large-scale deletion of voters in Delhi through SIR in the ASDD (absent, shifted, duplicate and dead) category, EC said those left out of the draft electoral rolls could submit fresh enumeration forms to electoral registration officers or assistant EROs at their current residential place."Electors who have not shifted may submit the signed enumeration form with the statement giving the reason for the earlier non-submission of the enumeration form. They can submit it to the ERO/AERO/BLO in person or through family members. Online submission option with e-sign will be available on ECINET," it said.Those Delhi voters who have shifted residence from one constituency to another can submit fresh enumeration forms along with address proof to the ERO/AERO or avail the option of 'book a call with BLO', it said."Enumeration forms submitted by such electors shall be processed by EROs in accordance with Rule 21(1) of Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and the same EPIC number shall be re-assigned to them. An elector who has already submitted Form 6 during the SIR need not submit the enumeration form afresh," EC said.
Article Summary: EC's stand, spelt out in an affidavit filed Saturday, is in sync with the Oct 26 assurance given by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. The CJI-led bench had said, "No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voters' lists"

Article Title: Mumbai physics forum hosts online lecture by Pak N-scientist
Article Text:
Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy (Courtesy: APLN)

MUMBAI: For the first time in recent years, Mumbai hosted an event on Sunday to honour a Pakistani scientist. The occasion was the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam and the event was an online lecture by eminent nuclear physicist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy, who spoke from Islamabad.The presentation, “The Truth About Abdus Salam: Science, Faith moved to and the Atom Bomb,’’ was organised by the Mumbai sub-regional council of the Indian Association of Physics Teachers. The audience comprised mainly physics teachers from different Mumbai colleges and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR). The interaction comes ahead of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue in Delhi in late Nov at which the federal Pakistani minister for climate change is expected to be present.Hoodbhoy, who described Salam as an ambassador for goodwill between India and Pakistan, stressed that while he was glad that the celebrated scientist was being recognised in India, it was not the same case in Pakistan as he belonged to the Ahmadiyya sect. “This is sad because there is no real role model for the youth of Pakistan right now,” he said.Hoodbhoy said Salam had a lot of interactions with Indian scientists and left behind a rich legacy.“Salam was a major figure in physics in the 20th century along with C.V. Raman and Jagdishchandra Bose,’’ he said.Hoodbhoy, a decorated scientist himself – a recipient of the Fulbright award in 1998 and the UNESCO Kalinga Prize in 2001 – said Salam played a key role in the initial years of research under former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto as Pakistan began work to develop nuclear weapons.’’
Article Summary: Mumbai hosted an event on Sunday to honour a Pakistani scientist. The occasion was the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam. The event was an online lecture by eminent nuclear physicist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy. He described Salam as an ambassador for goodwill between India and Pakistan.

Article Title: Faith, pollution and politics: How Yamuna takes centre stage every Chhath Puja
Article Text:
Significance of Chhath

Chhath and politics go hand in hand in Delhi

Why Chhath has become a political event

Why the Yamuna turns frothy around Chhath

The health risks for the devotees

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Purity, hygiene and cleanliness are paramount for devotees during Chhath Puja . With God as their witness - quite literally in this case - devotees go to great lengths to observe strict hygiene while following elaborate rituals centred around the worship of the Sun deity over four days.In Delhi, devotees stepped into the sullied waters of the Yamuna, believing that their faith will protect them.The festival also provided a political stage, with Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta joining devotees at the Yamuna ghats and offering prayers to Chhathi Maiya. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, too, extended his wishes on the occasion of Sandhya Arghya.But as thousands gathered along the river's banks, the Yamuna underwent its annual public audit - with devotees standing waist-deep in its waters.Chhath Puja, rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand.Observed over four days, the festival begins with Nahay-Khay, when devotees prepare simple, traditional food while observing strict personal hygiene and purity.This is followed by Kharna, when jaggery-based kheer and wheat rotis are prepared as prasad.After Kharna, devotees undertake a rigorous 36-hour nirjala fast, abstaining from both food and water.The rituals culminate in offerings of arghya to the setting Sun, followed by prayers to the rising Sun on the final day.Every year, as Chhath Puja approaches, the Yamuna becomes more than a river for Delhi.This year, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar, praising the cleanup under chief minister Rekha Gupta.“How can we not appreciate the work that has been done here?” he said. “There might be crocodiles in the water here, but crocodiles come in clean water.”AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar answered by floating an effigy of Tiwari at Kalindi Kunj and challenging him to bathe there, claiming that stretch was far more polluted.On Nahay Khay, the first day of the festival, a video purportedly showing dead fish near Sonia Vihar surfaced on social media.Delhi ministers accused AAP of staging it, alleging that party workers bought fish from the market and dumped them in the river.Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj denied this and demanded an inquiry on Friday, saying water samples had not yet been collected to establish the cause.The river has been a political flashpoint around Chhath before. Last year, AAP alleged that a temporary artificial pool at Vasudev Ghat was built to project a clean Yamuna ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s planned Chhath visit, which did not take place.Chhath's growing political importance has a lot to do with Delhi's changing demography. According to reports, continued migration from Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP has increased the share of the Purvanchali community to about 30 percent of Delhi's population.The festival offers political parties an opportunity to reach a sizeable constituency through a celebration deeply woven into its cultural identity.According to reports, the Delhi government is setting up 1,482 Chhath ghats across 996 locations. The growing prominence of a festival once largely observed within community networks reflects how it has become an important fixture on the capital's political calendar.The Yamuna's pollution becomes particularly visible around Chhath Puja, when devotees gather in large numbers along its banks to offer prayers.While talking to the Times of India, environmentalist Saumya Dutta said that the timing of Chhath coincides with a period when the river's flow has receded considerably after the monsoon, leaving less water to dilute the pollutants entering it.“During the days of Chhath Puja, tens of thousands of Delhi residents from Bihar and eastern UP, along with others, add huge amounts of pollutants, particularly detergents containing surfactants, which are common ingredients in soaps and detergents, as well as some industrial waste,” Dutta said.“Long after the peak monsoon flow, this is the period when the Yamuna's flow becomes very low. This low water flow, combined with high amounts of surfactants, causes large amounts of foam when the water is agitated. This becomes particularly visible during the huge influx of people and pollutants into this short 2% stretch of the Yamuna,” he said.According to Dutta, the 22-km stretch through the capital accounts for roughly 2% of the Yamuna's total length but contributes 70-80% of its overall pollution load.“Defaming agents and pre-Chhath cleaning do help for a very short period, but as the incoming pollution does not go down, this benefit is very short-term and vanishes quickly,” Dutta told TOI.“The major reason for the abject failure of Yamuna cleaning plans, as well as schemes like Namami Gange, is that the huge daily inflow of partially treated or even untreated sewage and industrial effluent into the river is not being tackled,” he added.In one of the most polluted major rivers of India, devotees will stand waist-deep, waiting for the Sun to set and rise the following day.But is it safe for a person to come in contact with such polluted river?According to Dr Srijan Garg immersion during Chhath can expose people to harmful bacteria, viruses and parasites through the skin, eyes, nose and ears, and sometimes through accidental ingestion."Devotees are exposed through the skin, eyes, nose, ear and sometimes by ingestion. However, the major exposure is through the skin and can cause various infections such as folliculitis, dermatitis, fungal infections," Dr. Garg told TOI.The water is full of untreated sewage water. so swallowing that water will affect the health of the individual. Some acute infections typhoid, hepatitis A or E, giardiasis, cholera. These usually present with diarrhoea, vomiting and pain abdomen," he added.Meanwhile, Dr. Ishan Singh said that people with cuts or open wounds are particularly vulnerable to infections."Industrial discharge may introduce heavy metals such as lead, mercury, arsenic and cadmium into river water. Depending on concentration and duration of exposure, these can affect the kidneys, liver and nervous system. Some chemicals may also irritate the skin and eyes," Dr. Singh told TOI."However, their actual presence and concentration at individual ghats must be confirmed through laboratory testing. A single brief exposure should not automatically be considered a cause of heavy-metal poisoning," he added.He also said that children, pregnant women, elderly people, diabetic patients and people with weakened immunity need particular attention.Dr. Singh also advised devotees to avoid swallowing river water, keep immersion time short and stay away from areas close to sewage discharge points. Those with open wounds should preferably avoid entering the water. After immersion, devotees should wash thoroughly with clean water and soap and change out of wet clothes.Chhath will end with prayers to the rising Sun, as devotees complete the four-day rituals with hopes and gratitude. However, the Yamuna's problems will remain long after the devotees leave the ghats.The wait for a cleaner river is likely to continue, with sewage and industrial waste flowing into it despite periodic cleaning drives and political promises.And when Chhath returns next year, the river will once again face its annual public audit, with the same questions over its cleanliness and safety likely to resurface.
Article Summary: Chhath Puja is rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya. It is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta joined devotees at the Yamuna ghats.

Article Title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype, seeks own industry
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: Kashmiri movie veterans have shined a harsh light on Bollywood’s trite scripts confining J&K’s depiction to “scenic beauty, skullcaps that few in the Valley actually wear and AK-47s carried under pherans and long beards”, while calling for strengthening indigenous filmmaking.Speakers reeled off such gripes at a seminar organised in Srinagar on Saturday by Kashmir Music Club, run by popular singer Waheed Jeelani.“We have stronger stories here and there is a need to develop them,” actor Umar Imtiyaz said as he took potshots at Bollywood for dishing out its familiar fare of “skullcaps, long beards and AK-47s under pherans (long, loose-fitting garments worn by Kashmiris in winter)”. Imtiyaz argued that it was time to challenge such stereotypical representations.Echoing the sentiment, filmmaker Ayash Arif called for a focus on regional cinema that blends local concerns with a broader global outlook. He criticised J&K govt’s film policy, arguing it was more of a tourism blueprint aimed at encouraging filmmakers from elsewhere to shoot in the region due to its scenic beauty. What is needed, Arif said, is a roadmap aimed at promoting local productions.The 2022 policy offers several initiatives, including a single-window portal for shooting permissions and subsidies.It recalls the heady 1960s when blockbusters like Kashmir Ki Kali, Jab Jab Phool Khile, Himalay Ki God Mein and Janwar were shot in Srinagar and Gulmarg, followed by some international productions such as The Razor’s Edge in the 1980s.At the seminar, however, many felt the policy does not address requirements back home. “There is a lot for outside filmmakers in the policy but not much for local makers,” Arif said.Director Kapil Matoo, whose recent film Tasrufdar: Djinns of Kashmir won critical acclaim, urged local filmmakers to shed a sense of victimhood and recognise their own potential. “We must have our own industry here and start making films as we have stories of every shade,” Matoo said.Actor-director Mir Sarwar exhorted local artists not to depend on the limited opportunities offered by Doordarshan Srinagar and J&K Academy of Art. “We must help each other rather than wait for roles from filmmakers who come from outside,” Sarwar said. Cinematographer Shafqat Habib felt Kashmiri filmmakers must carve out a distinct identity.
Article Summary: Kashmiri movie veterans have shined a harsh light on Bollywood’s trite scripts. Speakers reeled off such gripes at a seminar organised in Srinagar on Saturday. “We have stronger stories here and there is a need to develop them,” actor Umar Imtiyaz said.

Article Title: Air India Delhi-SFO was 2.5 hours away from destination when US ATC failed; all 5 AI flights landed on time
Article Text:
All 5 AI flights landed safely at their destinations and on time

Poll Vote & Share your view How concerned are you about air travel disruptions due to ground stops? Very concerned Somewhat concerned Not very concerned Not concerned at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Air India ’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination, when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th when Uncle Sam’s outdated air traffic control (ATC) systems began to fail. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. Luckily, the US Air Traffic Control System Command Centre (ATCSCC) advisory issued at 2.24 am (IST of Nov 14) to announce the ground stop said “inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis” while asking all departing flights to remain on ground. The Boeing 777 (VT-ALS) landed in SFO at 5 am.“As soon as the ATCSCC advisory was issued at 2.24 am, AI flight operations buzzed the leadership team and they went into a huddle. SFO flight was the closest to its destination and proceeded since the pilots, who were in touch with Oakland control at that time, were not told to divert as per the advisory which meant the B777 will be allowed to land,” said people in the know.AI kept a close eye on the developing situation and the four other flights — one each from Delhi and Mumbai to Newark (EWR) and JFK — kept proceeding to their destinations.The outage lasted about five hours and these all landed as per schedule.Of the five return flights these aircraft were to operate back home, only SFO-Delhi (via Kolkata) was delayed by about 2 hours and 40 minutes due to congestion at SFO. “All the other flights, two each out of EWR and JFK, operated on time,” said an official, adding Saturday-Sunday night departures were also on time except for the delayed arrival from SFO.AI senior pilots said this is the second time in less than four years that US faced an air traffic communication issue, although Friday the 13th was by far the most serious one. On Jan 10, 2023, the US Federal Aviation Administration was unable to issue notice to airmen (NOTAM) for some hours and it had to activate a hotline to manage the situation then. The FAA subsequently traced the problem to files unintentionally deleted by contract personnel while correcting synchronisation between the primary and backup databases.Following Friday’s failure, the US is prioritising international flights over domestic ones and the situation will take some days to recover as there will be a serious ripple effect. While Air India is the only Indian operator that flies to the US, two US carriers — United and American — have a daily each between Delhi and New York. Rest of the connectivity is provided by onestops of Gulf, European and southeast Asian carriers.Other airlines’ flights were also impacted.“Given the scale of the failure, the impact was massive. I was listening to ground control at JFK when the issue happened just before 4 pm EST (New York time) Friday. There were a lot of frustrated pilots and controllers. Hundreds of pilots were asking, ‘what’s the delay reason,’. Initially controller couldn’t give a reason and just said, ‘nationwide stop.’ Later it was determined a communication problem,” said a pilot who was in New York at that time.“Due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety, attention all aircraft operators: By order of the Federal Aviation Command Centre, all airports are ground stopped,” the ATCSCC advisory announcing the failure had said.
Article Summary: Air India’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. All 5 AI flights landed safely at their destinations and on time.

"I will write my own book and then you will come to know everything."Sonia Gandhi's response to former external affairs minister Natwar Singh's explosive autobiography in 2014 was as much a promise as it was a rebuttal. Singh's book had stirred a political storm with its account of why she declined the prime minister's post after the Congress-led UPA won the 2004 general elections. More controversially, he claimed that Rahul Gandhi had strongly opposed his mother's elevation, fearing she could meet the same fate as her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, both of whom were assassinated. Sonia, who had publicly attributed her decision to her "inner voice", was now promising to tell her side of the story.Twelve years later, that promise has come full circle. Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, was released on November 10, bringing her own account of her life, family and political journey into the public domain. The book has already triggered political reactions and renewed debate over some of the most contentious episodes involving the Gandhi family.But Sonia is hardly the first political figure to find that putting personal recollections on paper can have consequences far beyond the pages of a book.Over the years, memoirs by politicians have revisited ideological battles, exposed differences within parties, offered personal accounts of political turning points and reopened controversies that many thought had been settled.From L K Advani's account of the Jinnah controversy to Jayaprakash Narayan's prison diary during the Emergency, these books have offered glimpses into the people and decisions behind some of India's defining political moments.Here are five political memoirs that made headlines for what their authors chose to reveal.When Natwar Singh's autobiography was released in 2014, much of the attention centred on his account of Sonia Gandhi's decision not to become prime minister in 2004.While Sonia had publicly described the decision as a call of her "inner voice", Singh offered a different explanation. He claimed that Rahul Gandhi had strongly opposed his mother's elevation, fearing that she could meet the same fate as her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, both of whom were assassinated.Singh wrote that Rahul's opposition was so strong that he gave Sonia 24 hours to decide. He also claimed that he, Manmohan Singh, Suman Dubey and Priyanka Gandhi were present when Sonia struggled with the decision. According to him, Rahul's intervention ultimately led her to offer the post to Manmohan Singh.The memoir went beyond the 2004 episode. Singh offered a sharply critical assessment of Sonia's leadership and her control over the Congress, describing her as increasingly authoritarian and secretive. He also recounted conversations with former prime minister P V Narasimha Rao, who, according to Singh, was troubled by Sonia's attitude towards him.The revelations triggered a political storm. Sonia rejected Singh's account and announced that she would write her own book. Former prime minister Manmohan Singh dismissed the claims as a "marketing gimmick", while the Congress accused Natwar Singh of distorting facts to promote his book.The controversy deepened when Singh made remarks linking Sonia's alleged ruthlessness to her Italian origin, drawing further criticism.Released in New Delhi on March 19, 2008, by then President A P J Abdul Kalam, L K Advani's autobiography traced his journey from childhood in Karachi and Partition to his association with the RSS, the growth of the BJP, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and his years in the Union government.One of its most discussed sections revisited the controversy surrounding Advani's June 2005 visit to Pakistan and his remarks on Muhammad Ali Jinnah. During the visit, Advani praised Jinnah's August 11, 1947, address to Pakistan's Constituent Assembly, in which the latter spoke about religious freedom and equal citizenship irrespective of religion.The remarks triggered a backlash within the BJP and the Sangh Parivar. Sections of the party viewed them as a departure from its ideological position, and Advani eventually resigned as BJP president.Looking back at the episode, Advani described it as "simply the most agonising moment of my political life". He also recalled feeling let down by several party colleagues during the controversy, contrasting their response with the support he had received during the Hawala case in 1996.Explaining the purpose of his Pakistan visit, he wrote: "I went to Pakistan as a messenger of peace, with an earnest desire to contribute to the normalisation of relations between our two long-estranged nations."Advani maintained that he had not described Jinnah as secular but had referred to a particular speech as a "classic, a forceful espousal of a Secular State". He also argued that the media had reported his remarks without adequately explaining their historical context.The autobiography also revisited the 1990 Rath Yatra and the demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992. Another section offered insights into his long association with former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.While acknowledging that the two sometimes differed in their approaches, Advani wrote that he had always regarded Vajpayee as his leader and generally deferred to his opinion.Published in January 2012 by Roli Books, Mamata Banerjee's My Unforgettable Memories offered a personal account of the relationships, disappointments and political rivalries that shaped her career. The English book was a translation of excerpts from her earlier Bengali writings.It appeared just months after Mamata led the Trinamool Congress to a historic victory in the 2011 West Bengal assembly elections, ending the Left Front's 34-year rule. Her observations about prominent political figures, particularly Sonia Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, attracted considerable attention.Having spent years in the Congress before leaving the party to establish the Trinamool Congress in 1998, Mamata wrote about feeling repeatedly let down by its leadership. She referred to Sonia Gandhi as the "Queen Mother" and criticised the party's treatment of regional leaders."The culture in Congress is that when a regional faction gets too active, it's immediately censored by the top leadership," she wrote.Her account of Sonia, however, stood in contrast to the affection she expressed for Rajiv Gandhi, whom she described as "the leader of our hearts".Mamata recalled that after she was attacked at a rally in Kolkata in 1991 by alleged CPM activists, Rajiv took responsibility for arranging and paying for her treatment. He also sent people to ask whether she wanted to travel to the US for further medical care.She wrote that she was devastated when she heard of Rajiv's assassination in May 1991. She said she could neither eat nor speak to anyone for a week and described the loss as being "orphaned all over again, for the second time in my life since my father's death".The memoir also spoke warmly of former President Pranab Mukherjee, despite the changing political equations between the Congress and the Trinamool Congress."I have always respected him and my relationship with him is that of an elder brother and his kid sister," she wrote.She recalled that when Mukherjee was sidelined by the Congress and formed the Rashtriya Samajwadi Congress in 1986, she had repeatedly requested Rajiv Gandhi to take him back into the party.Unlike the other books, Jayaprakash Narayan's Prison Diary was not a retrospective account written years after the events. It was a record of his experiences during one of the most turbulent periods in India's democratic history: the Emergency.Popularly known as JP, Narayan was among the most prominent leaders of the movement against Indira Gandhi's government in the 1970s. His call for Sampoorna Kranti (Total Revolution) had brought together students, opposition parties and civil society groups.After the Allahabad high court set aside Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli on June 12, 1975, the movement gathered momentum. On June 25, JP addressed a massive rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, calling for a peaceful struggle against the government. Hours later, the Emergency was proclaimed. In the early hours of June 26, opposition leaders, including JP, were arrested.Written during his detention and published by Popular Prakashan in 1977, the diary documented his experiences in custody, his health, his reading and his reflections on the political crisis.One of its most striking passages appeared in the opening entry, dated July 21, 1975, nearly a month after his arrest. JP wrote, "My world lies in a shambles all round me."He went on to express disbelief that a democratically elected prime minister could use the law to undermine democracy and suppress political opposition. The diary also contained sharp criticism of the decision to impose the Emergency, arrest opposition leaders and curtail civil liberties.Another deeply personal aspect of the book was its account of JP's deteriorating health. He was 72 when arrested and was already facing health problems. During his detention, his kidneys failed. He was released on November 12, 1975, on medical grounds and subsequently required regular dialysis for the remaining years of his life.Published in the year the Emergency ended and the Janata Party came to power, Prison Diary offered a contemporary first-person account of the political crisis from one of its most prominent opponents.Former President Pranab Mukherjee's The Presidential Years (2012-2017) made headlines even before its release in December 2020. The book offered his assessment of the Congress's decline, his dealings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and some of the most consequential decisions taken during his presidency.Looking back at the Congress's defeat in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, when the party won just 44 seats, Mukherjee attributed its performance to several factors, including its failure to recognise the end of its charismatic leadership. He described the establishment as having been reduced to a "government of averages".His observations also touched upon the Congress's leadership under Sonia Gandhi and Manmohan Singh.The memoir was equally candid about his interactions with Modi during his five-year tenure as President. Mukherjee described their relationship as cordial and said he had regularly offered the prime minister advice on policy matters. However, he criticised the NDA government's handling of Parliament between 2014 and 2019, blaming its "arrogance and inept handling" for the acrimonious exchanges between the treasury and opposition benches, while holding the opposition responsible too.One of the most discussed revelations concerned demonetisation. Mukherjee disclosed that Modi had not consulted him before announcing the decision on November 8, 2016. He said the lack of prior consultation did not surprise him, as the element of surprise was essential to such an announcement.He recalled that Modi visited Rashtrapati Bhavan after announcing the decision and explained its rationale. Mukherjee described demonetisation as a bold step but warned that it could cause a temporary economic slowdown and that the government would have to be careful about easing the burden on the poor.The memoir also became the subject of a family disagreement. Mukherjee's son, former Congress MP Abhijit Mukherjee, asked the publisher to halt publication until he had reviewed the final manuscript and given written consent. His daughter Sharmistha Mukherjee opposed the demand, saying their father had completed the manuscript before falling ill and that the final draft retained his handwritten notes and comments.Accusing her brother of creating "unnecessary hurdles", Sharmistha said preventing the book's release would be the "greatest disservice" to their departed father. The disagreement played out on social media, adding a family feud to the political conversations surrounding the memoir.Political memoirs offer a rare window into the personal experiences and perspectives of those who have occupied positions of power. They can reveal ideological differences, internal party dynamics and relationships that rarely find space in official accounts.But they are also personal interpretations of history. The authors decide which episodes to revisit, which conversations to disclose and how to explain decisions made years earlier. And, as the controversies surrounding these books show, sometimes what a politician writes long after leaving office can reopen debates that their public life had never quite settled.
Article Summary: Political memoirs often bring long-held views, personal accounts and contested versions of history back into the spotlight. From L K Advani's account of the Jinnah controversy to Jayaprakash Narayan's prison diary during the Emergency, these books have offered glimpses into the people and decisions behind some of India's defining political moments.

Gadchiroli/Nagpur: Hope has returned to India's erstwhile Maoist heartland where tribal families once despaired at the prospect of armed groups snatching children from their mothers, abducting daughters from their homes and preventing people from even voting, PM Narendra Modi told a gathering in Gadchiroli Sunday as he basked in the "countless blessings" showered on his govt for "defeating Maoism and Naxalism".Addressing the Janjatiya Gaurav Divas event through video-conferencing on the 151st birth anniversary of Birsa Munda, PM Modi said the size of the turnout was testimony to people's appreciation of the govt's effort to end Maoist depredations in 125 districts across the country."As far as my eyes can see, there are people everywhere...The sister who now feels safe is blessing us. Article Title: 'Divide-and-rule tactics': RSS chief Bhagwat's warning over attempts to split India
Article Text:
Mohan Bhagwat at 'Maru Ninad-2026' in Jodhpur

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Sunday warned of attempts to divide India by exploiting smaller identities. He compared the efforts to the British-era policy of divide and rule and called for national unity.Addressing the 'Maru Ninad-2026' Ghosh Shivir organised by the RSS Jodhpur Prant at Rajaram Ashram in Shikarpura, Bhagwat said India was moving in the right direction. However, certain global forces did not want the country to become a great nation, ANI reported."India is the treasure trove of everyone's hopes. But the state of the world is very strange. For their own selfish reasons, they don't even want India to become great," Bhagwat said.He alleged that attempts were being made to create divisions by magnifying smaller identities and provoking conflicts among people. He compared these tactics to those used during British rule.The RSS chief urged people to shed selfishness, petty differences and ego. He stressed the need to build an organised society rooted in Dharma and national service.Citing the Mahabharata, Bhagwat explained how internal discord could weaken even a powerful force.He pointed out that the Kauravas had an army of 11 Akshauhinis and powerful warriors such as Bhishma, Dronacharya, Karna and Ashwatthama. Yet, they lost because of internal differences.In contrast, the Pandavas won with an army of seven Akshauhinis because they remained united and resolved their differences to preserve harmony, he said.Bhagwat also highlighted the importance of grassroots leadership. He said every village, street and neighbourhood needed 25 to 100 selfless individuals of good character who stood with people during their moments of happiness and sorrow and remained dedicated to the country.Speaking about the RSS Ghosh programme, Bhagwat traced the tradition of battlefield music to ancient Indian texts, including the Bhagavad Gita. He referred to the sacred conches Panchajanya and Devadatta, whose blowing marked the beginning of the Mahabharata war.He said early RSS volunteers initially learned musical compositions from British military bands. However, a sense of self-respect inspired them to develop original martial compositions based on Indian classical music theory.Bhagwat said RSS band performers did not play music for personal recognition or applause. Instead, the programme aimed to inculcate discipline, selflessness and teamwork and promote collective progress, he added.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat warns of attempts to divide India by exploiting smaller identities. He compared the efforts to the British-era policy of divide and rule. The RSS chief urged people to shed selfishness, petty differences and ego. He stressed the need to build an organised society rooted in Dharma.

NEW DELHI: Amid speculation over a possible alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party ahead of the Punjab assembly polls, Akali Dal leader Daljit Singh Cheema said the party had entrusted its president, Sukhbir Singh Badal , with the responsibility of forging an alliance with any party in the interest of the state.Speaking to reporters, Cheema said the final decision on an alliance would be taken by Badal."We have entrusted the party president with the responsibility of forming an alliance with any party for the welfare of Punjab," the veteran leader said."The final decision will be taken by Sukhbir Singh Badal," he added.This comes days after TOI reported that an alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP was on the cards.According to the report, the BJP is likely to contest a substantially higher number of seats than it did under its earlier seat-sharing arrangement with the regional outfit.BJP sources said the alliance would be announced at an opportune time. Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: 'Abusive language': Yashveer Goud reveals why India celebrated fiercely after U19 Asia Cup final win over Pakistan
Article Text:
Image credit: BCCI

'Return bhi dena padta hai'

India bounce back to beat Pakistan in dramatic final

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's celebrations after winning the U19 Asia Cup final against Pakistan were full of emotion. Now, young batter Yashveer Goud has revealed what led to the players' reactions after the memorable victory. Goud claimed that there was an exchange of words, including abusive language, when India lost to Pakistan in the group stage on Diwali."We had lost the match on Diwali. There was some exchange of words between us, including abusive language. We couldn't say anything after losing that match. We were waiting for the final. We wanted to perform well and show what India is capable of," Goud told Sports Today.Goud also explained why the Indian players celebrated the way they did after winning the final. According to him, they wanted to respond in the same manner as their Pakistani opponents had reacted after the group-stage match."We were doing the same thing they had done. They were silent and we were silent too. We were wearing the proud Indian jersey. We were waiting for this moment. Return bhi dena padta hai. Everyone was emotional," he added.India had lost to Pakistan by three wickets in the group stage despite scoring 208.The defeat came on Diwali, making the loss even more disappointing for the young Indian team.India had posted 208 in the group-stage match, with Arjun Rajput scoring an unbeaten 107 off just 85 balls. However, Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten 100 helped Pakistan recover from 61/5 and complete a three-wicket victory.India bounced back strongly in the semi-finals, beating Afghanistan by eight wickets. Captain Lakshya Raichandani led the way with 93 runs to set up another meeting with Pakistan in the final.Pakistan produced a strong batting performance in the title clash, scoring 337/9. Usman Khan led the charge with 107, while Abdul Qadir scored 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf contributed 63.India started their chase well, with Raichandani scoring 80 and Aaryavir Sehwag making 58. However, Pakistan fought back and left India struggling at 252/8.Manal Chauhan kept India's hopes alive with 47 off 32 balls. But his dismissal at 309/9 left Mohit Ulva with just one wicket remaining.Ulva kept his calm and found support from Chigurupati Venkata. The pair added 30 runs for the last wicket to take India across the finish line. Ulva remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 balls as India reached 339/9 to register a thrilling one-wicket victory on the final ball.The win helped India dethrone Pakistan as U19 Asia Cup champions and completed a memorable comeback after their group-stage defeat.
Article Summary: India beat Pakistan by one wicket in the U19 Asia Cup final. Young batter Yashveer Goud has revealed what led to the players' reactions after the memorable victory. Goud claimed that there was an exchange of words, including abusive language, when India lost to Pakistan in the group stage on Diwali.

NEW DELHI: The International Cricket Council (ICC) Board has announced the unopposed reappointment of Jay Shah for a second term as ICC Chair.The decision was taken following a proposal by ICC Directors at the Board and Committee meetings in Bali.The reappointment reflects the Board's confidence in Shah's leadership and ensures continuity at a crucial juncture for the sport, with global expansion, growing fan engagement and commercial development among the key priorities on the ICC's strategic roadmap.“I am deeply honoured by the confidence the ICC Board has placed in me and sincerely grateful to every Director for their continued trust and support. Serving as Chair of the ICC is both a privilege and a responsibility, and I remain committed to working with our Members to advance the interests of cricket across the world," Jay Shah said in a statement.“We are entering one of the most important and exciting periods in our sport’s history. Cricket’s return to the Olympic Games at LA28 presents an extraordinary opportunity to introduce our game to new audiences and inspire a new generation of players and fans.“Our responsibility extends well beyond delivering successful events. We must build a stronger and more sustainable future for the sport with a focus on fans, athletes, commercial partners and other key stakeholders.“I have always believed that cricket’s greatest strength lies in its ability to bring people together. With the support of the Board and our Members, our focus will be on turning ambition into action and ensuring that the progress we make leaves a lasting legacy for generations to come.”Shah was first elected unopposed as ICC chairman in 2024. He took over from Greg Barclay, who decided not to seek a third term.Jay Shah became the youngest chairperson in the ICC's history. He is the fifth Indian to head the governing body after Jagmohan Dalmiya, Sharad Pawar, N Srinivasan and Shashank Manohar.The 38-year-old has also served as the honorary secretary of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and chairperson of the Asian Cricket Council (ACC).In 2019, Shah was elected as the youngest-ever honorary secretary of the BCCI. During his tenure, Indian cricket witnessed several significant developments, including the record-breaking IPL media rights deal, the launch of the Women's Premier League (WPL), the establishment of the state-of-the-art Centre of Excellence and the introduction of the Test Cricket Incentive Scheme.Shah's journey in cricket administration began in 2009 at the district and state levels, before he quickly rose through the ranks of the Gujarat Cricket Association (GCA).
Article Summary: Shah was first elected unopposed as ICC chairman in 2024. He took over from Greg Barclay, who decided not to seek a third term. The 38-year-old has also served as the honorary secretary of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and chairperson of the Asian Cricket Council.

Article Title: How did Jaden Agassi step out of his famous parents' shadow? Meet Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf's son chasing a baseball dream
Article Text:
How did Jaden Agassi step out of his famous parents' shadow? Meet Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf's son chasing a baseball dream

Who is Jaden Agassi, the son of Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf?

Why did Jaden Agassi choose baseball over tennis?

How did Jaden Agassi build his baseball career at USC?

Why did Jaden Agassi represent Germany in the World Baseball Classic?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jaden Agassi grew up with one of the most famous surnames in tennis, but he has chosen a very different sport to build his career. The 25-year-old son of Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf has developed into a baseball pitcher, played college baseball at the University of Southern California (USC) and represented Germany in the 2025 World Baseball Classic qualifiers. While his parents won a combined 30 Grand Slam singles titles, Jaden has no plans to recreate their achievements on the tennis court. Instead, he wants to give the Agassi name a place in baseball.Born on October 26, 2001, Jaden Gil Agassi is the first child of Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf. His parents married just days before his birth and welcomed their daughter, Jaz Elle Agassi, on October 3, 2003.Growing up in Las Vegas, Jaden had two parents who understood what it meant to compete at the highest level. Andre won eight Grand Slam singles titles, while Steffi collected 22. Together, they became one of the most successful couples in tennis history.However, their sporting achievements did not mean their children had to follow the same route. Andre and Steffi largely kept Jaden and Jaz away from public attention during their childhood. They wanted their children to have the freedom to enjoy their interests without constantly being compared with their famous parents.Andre has also spoken about how his own childhood influenced the way he raised his children. In his autobiography, Open, he described the demanding training and expectations he faced under his father. He did not want Jaden and Jaz to grow up feeling that they had to become professional athletes to make their parents happy.The couple followed that approach when it came to choosing sports, too. Steffi once explained their decision, saying, “We never really introduced tennis so much into their lives. They’ve chosen other things.”Jaden discovered baseball when he was six years old, and he quickly became attached to the game. Although he had plenty of opportunities to try tennis, he never felt the same connection with it.In an interview with MLB.com, Jaden explained what made baseball the right choice for him.“I started playing baseball when I was six years old in T-ball,” he said. “I loved it. I’ve picked up a tennis racket a good amount, but it was always hard for me to keep that ball in between the lines. I just wanted to hit that thing as far as I could. Baseball had my love since day one.”His decision was not about moving away from his family’s sporting background. He simply found something he enjoyed more.Jaden also inherited a few qualities from his parents that have helped him as a pitcher. He has credited his mother for the calm approach he takes when facing pressure during games.“I think I’m a lot like my mom in the sense of my composure,” he said. “I’ve always been just very composed and cool, calm and collected out there. I try to have a short memory. My mindset is the next pitch is the most important one.”That approach is particularly important for a pitcher, who has to put a difficult moment behind him and focus on the next batter.Jaden’s journey in baseball has not always been easy. After playing on travel teams during his freshman and sophomore years of high school, he suffered an elbow injury during his first outing for Palo Verde High School in Las Vegas. The injury required Tommy John surgery, forcing him to miss the entire 2019 season.His return to the sport was also affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, which brought his 2020 season to an early end. This meant he had limited playing time before beginning his college career.Jaden eventually joined the University of Southern California, where he continued developing as a pitcher while studying Business Administration. The experience gave him an opportunity to work with coaches and improve his understanding of the game.Speaking to MLB.com, he explained how much he still had to learn when he arrived at USC.“I entered college with the ability to be a decent pitcher, but I was a thrower,” he said. “And because of lost time I was behind the eight ball. But at USC I was blessed with some great coaches who began teaching me the art of pitching.”His development continued beyond college. In 2023, he played for the Santa Barbara Foresters in the California Collegiate League before joining the Mahoning Valley Scrappers of the MLB Draft League in 2024.That season proved important for his progress. According to MLB.com, Jaden recorded a 2.96 ERA and 9.2 strikeouts per nine innings with the Scrappers. He also received Player of the Week honours on July 8, 2024.These performances gave him another opportunity to show what he could do as a pitcher after the setbacks earlier in his career.One of the biggest steps in Jaden’s baseball journey came in February 2025, when he joined Team Germany for the World Baseball Classic qualifiers in Tucson, Arizona.Although he was born and raised in the United States, Jaden has a connection to Germany through his mother, Steffi Graf, who was born in the country. He holds German citizenship and has visited his mother’s family there while growing up.His selection also gave him an opportunity to represent the country that has been part of his family background for generations.Major League Baseball reported his inclusion in the German team on February 14, 2025. The move was another important step for Jaden, who had been working towards competing at the international level.He had also made his ambitions clear when speaking about his famous surname. In an interview with WKBN News, he said, “Agassi is a very tennis last name, of course. The goal is to try to make it a baseball one.”That statement sums up what he wants to achieve. Rather than being known only as the son of two tennis champions, Jaden wants people to recognise him for his own work on a baseball field.His father has also supported his decision to choose a different sport. Andre and Steffi have consistently made it clear that their children should have the freedom to decide what they want to do.Jaden’s recent appearance at Roland-Garros offered another glimpse into the family. On June 5, 2026, he joined Andre at the men’s semifinals of the French Open in Paris. Photographs published by Getty Images showed the father and son attending the match together.The appearance also brought attention to how much Jaden has grown since his childhood days. Now 25, he is continuing to follow a sporting path that looks very different from the careers of his parents.For Jaden, the aim is not to match Andre Agassi’s eight Grand Slam titles or Steffi Graf’s 22. He wants to establish himself in baseball and give the Agassi surname a new sporting identity.
Article Summary: Jaden Gil Agassi is the first child of Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf. The 25-year-old grew up in Las Vegas. He played college baseball at the University of Southern California. He represented Germany in the 2025 World Baseball Classic qualifiers.

Article Title: Ed Kelce’s love and sacrifices shaped Jason and Travis Kelce’s NFL journey, but his greatest legacy lies in the love that held their family together
Article Text:
Ed Kelce’s love and sacrifices shaped Jason and Travis Kelce’s NFL journey, but his greatest legacy lies in the love that held their family together

How Ed Kelce helped Jason and Travis Kelce discover their love for sports

The sacrifices Ed and Donna Kelce made to support their sons

How Ed Kelce and Donna Kelce put their children first despite marriage problems

Ed Kelce never stopped supporting Jason and Travis after their NFL success

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Behind NFL stars Jason and Travis Kelce ’s success is a father who spent years making sure they had the support to follow their dreams. Ed Kelce coached them, encouraged their love for sports and made personal sacrifices to give them better opportunities. Even when his marriage with Donna Kelce faced difficulties, he continued putting his sons first. His journey shows how much a parent’s support can matter in a child’s life.Ed Kelce grew up in Cleveland, Ohio, where he developed an interest in football and baseball. Having played both sports himself, he understood how much they could teach children. When Jason and Travis were young, he wanted them to enjoy sports without feeling forced to follow a particular path.He started getting involved when the boys were very little. Ed coached Travis in T-ball and Jason in coach-pitch baseball. He also spent time playing with them in the front yard and created space in the family garage where they could practise.One of his favourite memories goes back to when Jason was still a toddler. His son would roll a ball towards him on the living-room floor, and Ed would roll it back. It was a simple activity, but it became one of their earliest shared memories.Years later, while appearing on the brothers’ New Heights podcast, Ed explained how he viewed his responsibility as a father.“My job is to help you find a passion, and then feed that passion. Whatever you want to do, I’m there.”He wanted both boys to discover what they enjoyed and then work towards becoming better at it. He also believed that talent needed to be supported by hard work. Rather than always placing them in situations where they could easily succeed, he encouraged them to compete and learn from more difficult experiences.That approach helped Jason and Travis develop their interest in football. Both eventually attended the University of Cincinnati, where they played college football before entering the NFL.Raising two children with serious sporting ambitions required time, money and a lot of planning. Jason and Travis played different sports and had busy schedules, so their parents had to manage practices, competitions, travel and equipment costs.Ed worked in the steel industry before moving into sales, while Donna built her career in banking. Both had professional responsibilities, but they made sure their sons received the support they needed.The financial side was not always easy. The family had to plan its spending around the boys’ sporting activities, including equipment, travel and other expenses. Ed and Donna had to make choices to ensure both children could take part in the activities they enjoyed.They also divided their parenting responsibilities carefully. Donna explained on New Heights that they worked as a team. When one parent travelled with Jason for a game, the other stayed home with Travis. This allowed both boys to receive attention and support, even when their schedules clashed.Donna described their arrangement as being “like a tag team with you two.”It was not always possible for both parents to attend every event, but they made sure someone was there. Their priority was to give Jason and Travis equal opportunities rather than allowing one child’s sporting commitments to take over family life.Neither Ed nor Donna knew that their sons would eventually become NFL stars. They were simply making sure the boys had the chance to explore their interests and work towards their goals.While Ed and Donna were busy raising their sons, their own marriage was going through a difficult period. The couple had been married for nearly 25 years, but their relationship was not always happy.Travis spoke about this in the Prime Video documentary Kelce. He remembered noticing during childhood that his parents did not share a bedroom. As he reached middle school, he began to understand that their marriage was struggling.Despite their personal problems, Ed and Donna continued raising their sons together. They knew that separating while Jason and Travis were still studying and playing sports would make an already busy family life more difficult.Ed explained their decision in the documentary, saying, “If we had split as we probably both would have preferred, that would have been a nightmare with the logistics, getting kids where they had to be and providing all the support.”His words give an idea of the practical challenges they were trying to avoid. They had to manage school, sports, travel and other family responsibilities, and both understood how much their sons depended on them.Their marriage eventually ended in divorce after Jason and Travis had graduated from college. However, their separation did not end their responsibilities as parents. They continued to support their sons and remained connected as a family.Donna has also spoken warmly about Ed and their years together, making it clear that she does not regret the family they built.Ed’s involvement did not end when his sons left home for college. When Jason joined the Philadelphia Eagles and Travis became a star with the Kansas City Chiefs, he continued attending games and following their careers.Supporting both sons became more challenging once they started playing for different NFL teams. Their games were often held in different cities, making it difficult for Ed and Donna to be present at every match. They continued dividing their time so both brothers could receive support.One of the most memorable moments came during Super Bowl LVII in February 2023, when Jason’s Eagles faced Travis’s Chiefs. It was an unusual situation for the family because one son would celebrate winning the championship while the other would have to deal with defeat.Ed understood how difficult that could be. Before the game, he explained that he wanted to be with whichever son lost.“Somebody’s gonna feel pretty crummy and I wanna be with him-initially.”He also joked that he had already won because both his sons had reached the Super Bowl.The game ended with Travis and the Chiefs defeating Jason and the Eagles 38-35. Ed and Donna celebrated with Travis but also had to share the difficult moment with Jason.For Ed, the journey was about much more than watching his sons become famous football players. He had been there when they first started playing sports, helped them through their childhood and continued supporting them when their careers reached the highest level.His story is a reminder that behind many successful athletes are parents who make sacrifices without knowing where their children’s dreams will eventually lead.
Article Summary: Ed Kelce coached Jason and Travis Kelce when they were young. He wanted them to enjoy sports without feeling forced to follow a particular path. Ed and Donna Kelce made sacrifices to give their sons better opportunities. Even when their marriage was going through difficulties, he continued putting his sons first.

Article Title: Pune airline staffer found stabbed to death in Gondia forest, male friend's robbery story raises suspicion

NAGPUR: The mysterious death of 35-year-old Varsha Turkar, who worked with a private airline at Pune airport, has left investigators puzzled, with police suspecting foul play after she was found stabbed in a secluded forest in Gondia district on Saturday evening.The victim's male companion, who claimed that masked robbers had attacked them and robbed them of Rs 40,000 in cash and gold valuables, has been detained for questioning as investigators found his version of events suspicious.Varsha was employed at the airline's ticket counter at Pune airport and lived in the Dhanori area. She had travelled with her two-and-a-half-year-old daughter to her maternal home in Navegaon Kinhi village in Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district to celebrate Diwali. She was supposed to return to Pune on Sunday.According to police, Varsha left home around 4pm on Saturday with her acquaintance, Nitesh Agrawal, a resident of Manohar Chowk in Gondia.The two had gone to the Bondrani forest area near the Wainganga river, behind a temple.Agrawal later told her family that three unidentified men attacked them after they got out of their car. He claimed that one of the assailants stabbed Varsha with a knife during an attempted robbery.However, the circumstances surrounding the incident raised questions. Agrawal escaped without any injuries, while Varsha suffered four deep stab wounds on her back.Relatives rushed her to Khairlanji hospital, where doctors declared her dead around 7pm.Dawaniwada police have detained Agrawal and are questioning him to verify his claims.A dog squad has been deployed, while investigators are examining both murder and robbery angles. Her father has demanded a fair investigation. No arrests have been made so far.
Article Summary: Varsha Turkar, 35, was found stabbed in a secluded forest in Gondia district. Her male companion claimed that masked robbers had attacked them and robbed them of Rs 40,000 in cash and gold valuables. Varsha was employed at the airline's ticket counter at Pune airport.

Article Title: Teenager Mirra Andreeva joins elite group of tennis stars after winning WTA Finals without losing a single set
Article Text:
Mirra Andreeva (AP Photo)

Andreeva joins elite group of tennis stars

Svitolina praises Andreeva after final
