NEW DELHI: Russian tennis star Mirra Andreeva capped off a remarkable season by winning the WTA Finals without losing a single set. The 19-year-old defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday's final to finish the tournament with five wins from five matches.The victory also helped Andreeva reach a career-best world ranking of No. 2, behind Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina.Along with the title, Andreeva earned $3.37 million in prize money and a unique ultraviolet purple Mercedes-Benz convertible. However, there is one thing she still needs before she can drive her new car: a driver's license.“This is an amazing motivation for me to get my driver's license as fast as I can,” she said. “If not, then look, I have five people on my team. I'm going to be a passenger's princess forever, that's also an option for me.”With this victory, Andreeva became only the 11th player to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set. She joined legendary names such as Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Serena Williams.Speaking after her win, the teenager expressed her happiness at joining such an elite group.“I'm super privileged to put my name in that group,” she said.Andreeva also took a moment to appreciate her own hard work during the awards ceremony. Wearing a jacket with the words 'I want to thank myself', she spoke about the effort and dedication behind her success.“I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day and for committing to what I have to do,” she said. “Just thanks to myself without any reason.”The final was closely fought, with both players exchanging breaks and battling hard from the baseline. However, Andreeva won five of the last six games to seal the title in just under two hours.The match ended after Svitolina missed an easy smash, giving Andreeva the victory. The players did not shake hands after the match, continuing the practice followed by Ukrainian players against Russian and Belarusian opponents since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.Despite the situation, Andreeva congratulated Svitolina on her season and praised her comeback as a mother.“You're an amazing mom to come back and do this. It's super hard,” she said. “I just wish you the best of luck for the next season.”Svitolina also acknowledged Andreeva's performance, saying, “I put everything out there and she played incredible.”
Article Summary: Russian tennis star Mirra Andreeva won the WTA Finals without losing a set. The 19-year-old defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday's final. She earned $3.37 million in prize money and a unique ultraviolet purple Mercedes- Benz convertible.

Article Title: Dianna Russini opens up about 'heartbreaking' six months after Mike Vrabel scandal, reveals how NFL players urged her to return
Article Text:
Dianna Russini (Getty Images)

How did Dianna Russini spend her months away from NFL reporting?

Why did Dianna Russini and Kevin Goldschmidt delete their social media accounts?

How did NFL players support Dianna Russini during her break?

What happened between Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dianna Russini has opened up about the difficult months she spent away from sports media after the controversy involving New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. The former NFL reporter said staying at her New Jersey home with her husband, Kevin Goldschmidt, and their two sons gave her a chance to rethink her priorities and focus on her family. Now, seven months after leaving The Athletic, Russini has returned to football coverage with a new show, The Russini Report, on BetUS TV. During its November 11 debut, she also spoke about the support she received from NFL players and people around the league.Russini began the first episode of her new show with a personal message about the time she spent away from work. Rather than going straight into football news, she spoke about how being at home helped her look at her life differently.“Over the last few months, I have had a lot of time to think about my life and my priorities and the person that I want to be moving forward, and being home in New Jersey with my husband and our two little boys and being truly present, it gave me so much perspective that I didn’t even know I needed,” Russini said.Her comments offered a glimpse into how she spent the months following her departure from The Athletic. The reporter, who had been a familiar face in NFL coverage, stepped away from her regular work after photographs of her with Vrabel at an Arizona resort became public.The time away also allowed her to spend more time with Goldschmidt and their children. Russini did not go into every detail of what happened during those months, but made it clear that being with her family had become an important part of her life.The months following the controversy were particularly difficult for Russini and her husband. Both decided to delete their X accounts after finding it increasingly hard to deal with the comments and claims being made about them online.In an interview with PEOPLE, Russini explained why they chose to step away from social media. She did not want the online discussion to become another problem for her family while they were already dealing with a difficult situation.“This was a runaway train, and there was nothing I could do to stop it. Once we realized nothing was going to stop this, it became unhealthy for us to read it because it wasn’t helping us heal. It was piling on and adding to what we were already dealing with.”She also spoke about the emotional effect of the entire episode, saying, “The best way to describe what the last six months were like for me is heartbreaking.”Russini had earlier described the situation as a nightmare. Her decision to stay away from social media gave her and Goldschmidt some distance from the constant discussion surrounding the photographs.Although Russini stepped away from her regular reporting work, she said she did not lose contact with people in the NFL. In fact, she credited the league and its players with helping her feel connected to football during a period when she was not working.She said people from the NFL regularly checked on her, not just to discuss football but also to ask how she was doing personally.“The absolute best part of this situation has been the loyalty the NFL has shown me. They checked in with me almost daily while I wasn’t working to make sure that I was staying connected to football, to check on me as a person and to just see how I was doing,” she said.Russini also revealed that several players contacted her directly and encouraged her to return to work. Their messages meant a lot to her, especially because she had spent years reporting on athletes who faced difficult moments in their careers.“I felt like players were texting and calling me to say, ‘Get back to work, it’s time,’” she said.She then explained how those conversations changed the way she looked at her own situation.“I think it’s pretty poetic that here I was all these years telling the story about these players going through adversity, and then they became sort of the people that I was learning from during this,” she added.For someone who had spent much of her career reporting on the NFL, hearing those words from players gave her another reason to return to the job.The controversy began after Page Six published photographs of Russini and Mike Vrabel together at the Ambiente resort in Sedona, Arizona. The pictures, taken on March 28, 2026, showed the NFL reporter and the Patriots coach hugging, holding hands and spending time together near the resort’s pool and hot tub.Both initially pushed back against suggestions that anything inappropriate had happened. Vrabel told the New York Post, “These photos show a completely innocent interaction and any suggestion otherwise is laughable. This doesn’t deserve any further response.”Russini also defended the photographs, saying, “The photos don’t represent the group of six people who were hanging out during the day. Like most journalists in the NFL, reporters interact with sources away from stadiums and other venues.”However, the situation became more difficult for Russini after The Athletic began an internal investigation into the matter. On April 14, she announced her resignation before her contract was due to end on June 30.In her resignation letter to executive editor Steven Ginsberg, she wrote, “I have covered the NFL with professionalism and dedication throughout my career, and I stand behind every story I have ever published.”She also explained her decision to leave, writing, “I do so not because I accept the narrative that has been constructed around this episode, but because I refuse to lend it further oxygen or to let it define me or my career.”The Athletic completed its investigation in September. As reported by Reuters, the outlet said Russini should have disclosed the nature of her relationship with Vrabel so editors could assess whether any reporting assignments involved a possible conflict of interest.Vrabel also addressed the situation publicly. In April, he announced that he would seek counseling and spend time with his family. He said, “I have always wanted to lead by example, and I believe this is what I have to do to be the best husband, father and coach that I possibly can be.”Russini’s return to sports media marks a new professional chapter. Her first show faced technical problems and started around 45 minutes late, with BetUS blaming the delay on a record-breaking audience. Once the programme began, she focused on NFL discussions rather than directly addressing the controversy.Her new show will cover NFL news, game analysis and her personal opinions, giving her a different way to continue working in football.
Article Summary: Dianna Russini has opened up about the difficult months she spent away from sports media after the controversy involving New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. The former NFL reporter said staying at her New Jersey home with her husband, Kevin Goldschmidt, and their two sons gave her a chance to rethink her priorities and focus on her family. She also spoke about the support she received from NFL players and people around the league.

Bangladesh produced a remarkable fightback against South Africa on the opening day of the Test at The Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg on Sunday. After losing three wickets for just 22 runs, the visitors recovered through a brilliant century from Towhid Hridoy and an unbeaten 92 from Litton Das to reach 327/6 at stumps.The total is now Bangladesh's highest in a Test innings against South Africa, surpassing their previous best of 326, scored in Chattogram in 2015.Bangladesh had also scored 320 in Potchefstroom in 2017, which was their second-highest total against the Proteas.With four wickets still in hand, Bangladesh have already gone past the 300-run mark for only the fourth time in their Test history against South Africa. Their scoring rate of 3.89 runs per over also reflects how positively they batted after the early collapse.The biggest moment of the day came through Hridoy and Litton, who put together an unbeaten partnership of 206 runs for the sixth wicket. It is the highest partnership by a Bangladesh pair against South Africa for any wicket.The stand came after Kagiso Rabada's fiery new-ball spell had put the visitors under serious pressure. The fast bowler reduced Bangladesh to 22/3 in the ninth over before striking twice again after lunch to leave them struggling at 121/5.However, Hridoy and Litton changed the course of the innings with a combination of patience and attacking shots. They kept the scoreboard moving and made full use of the older ball to put South Africa's bowlers under pressure.Hridoy brought up his fifty off 99 balls, while Litton reached his half-century off 71 deliveries. The pair added 94 runs in 20 overs before the second new ball became available.Hridoy's century was another major achievement in his young Test career. He became only the second Bangladesh batter to score a Test hundred against South Africa, after Mahmudul Hasan Joy, who achieved the feat in 2022.The 26-year-old reached the milestone in only his fourth Test. He has been in outstanding form, having scored an unbeaten 242 against West Indies just 10 days ago. That remains the highest individual score by a Bangladesh batter.Hridoy showed great patience against a South African attack that generated pace, bounce and movement. He reached his hundred off a Dane Paterson delivery that climbed towards him. The batter leaned back and guided it through backward point for four before celebrating with both arms raised and performing sajda on the field.His innings eventually ended on exactly the same score as Mahmudul's century against South Africa. Marco Jansen trapped him leg-before-wicket after the hosts took the second new ball. Hridoy reviewed the decision, but the original verdict stood.Rabada was the pick of the South African bowlers, claiming his 18th five-wicket haul in Test cricket. He moved level with Makhaya Ntini at joint-third on South Africa's all-time list.Only Dale Steyn (26) and Allan Donald (20) have taken more five-wicket hauls for South Africa.However, the hosts will be disappointed with the support Rabada received from the other bowlers. No other South African bowler managed a wicket until the final ball of the day.Paterson, playing his first Test since Boxing Day 2024, troubled the batters and forced several edges but failed to take a wicket. Jansen struggled to find the right length, while Wiaan Mulder could not create much pressure. Specialist spinner Simon Harmer also proved expensive, conceding runs at 5.18 per over.Bangladesh's decision to bat first after captain Shanto won the toss looked risky on a pitch with a good covering of grass. Their start made things worse as debutant opener Mahfijul Islam was dismissed off the first ball of the match.He became only the fourth player in Test history to register a first-ball duck on debut. Mahfijul went after a full delivery outside off stump from Rabada and edged it to Jansen at gully.Mominul Haque survived the rest of the opening over but fell for a duck in Rabada's next over, edging the ball to the wicketkeeper.Rabada then removed Shanto with another excellent delivery. The batter was tempted into a drive, but the ball moved through the gap between bat and pad before hitting the off stump.Tanzid Hasan and Hridoy then stopped the slide with a 69-run partnership. Bangladesh went to lunch at 91/3 and added another 30 runs after the break before Rabada returned to strike. Tanzid, who had scored 67, played a back-of-a-length delivery onto his stumps. Mushfiqur Rahim followed in the same over, edging Rabada to Harmer at third slip. The wicket completed Rabada's five-wicket haul.Rabada came close to taking a hat-trick when his next delivery moved away from Litton, but the batter managed to guide it towards point and survive.Litton and Hridoy gradually took control with positive batting. Litton pulled a short delivery from Jansen fine for four, while Hridoy used his back foot to hit Mulder through midwicket.Hridoy brought up his half-century off 99 balls, and Bangladesh went into tea at 184/5 without losing another wicket. The pair continued their attacking approach in the final session. Litton punched Paterson down the ground for four before reaching his half-century off 71 balls with an outside edge against Rabada.Hridoy also moved closer to his century as Bangladesh took advantage of the older ball. South Africa appeared to be waiting for the second new ball, and the visitors made the most of that period, scoring 94 runs in 20 overs before it became available.South Africa also reviewed two leg-before appeals against Hridoy during Rabada's spell, but both decisions went in the batter's favour as the impact was outside off stump.The second new ball eventually ended Hridoy's brilliant innings, but Bangladesh had already completed a remarkable recovery. From 22/3 and later 121/5, they finished the opening day at 327/6, putting themselves in a strong position and recording their highest-ever Test total against South Africa.
Article Summary: Bangladesh reach 327/6 at stumps on opening day of Test against South Africa. Towhid Hridoy scored 137 off 227 balls, while Litton Das made 92. The total is now Bangladesh's highest in a Test innings against the Proteas. Kagiso Rabada took three wickets for just 22 runs on the opening day.

Article Title: 'Who is this cocky little guy?': Dale Steyn's first impression of young Virat Kohli
Article Text:
Royal Challengers Bengaluru's Virat Kohli, left, with former cricketer and commentator Dale Steyn (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former South African fast bowler Dale Steyn has recalled his first impression of a young Virat Kohli , admitting that the Indian batting star initially struck him as a rather cocky youngster during the 2008 Under-19 World Cup. However, their subsequent association at Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) brought the two closer, with a shared love for food and music helping them develop a strong off-field bond. Steyn was speaking alongside former South African captain Faf du Plessis on ESPNcricinfo's show 'Cricketers on Cricketers', where he looked back at his early interactions with Kohli and the Indian's transformation into one of the biggest names in world cricket.The former pacer, who represented RCB during the first three IPL seasons from 2008 to 2010, recalled watching India defeat South Africa in the Under-19 World Cup final in 2008. Kohli had captained India to the title, and Steyn, who had been following the tournament, was left with a rather strong first impression of the youngster."I actually remember watching the Under-19 World Cup. We had a tour of India. Sehwag had just smashed us.He scored 300 in Chennai in a day (in 2008). We had had a tour somewhere else, maybe just before that. I think we had even gone to Bangladesh just before that. I remember watching India beat South Africa U-19s in the [2008] World Cup, and India stormed the field. And I saw this kid, and I was like, who's this cocky little bloody s***? You know? And the next thing I find out, he's actually in my team," Steyn said.The South African admitted that he initially wondered how he would deal with the youngster when they became teammates at RCB. However, his perception changed once they got to know each other, as the two discovered several common interests away from cricket."He is with us at RCB. And I'm like, oh my goodness. I gotta deal with this little guy, you know? Anyway, it turns out when I met him, we had a lot of common interests. We were young, and we enjoyed a little bit of an off-the-field kind of enjoyment in life. We used to go to all the restaurants and stuff that Bangalore had to offer - Hard Rock Cafe was a particular favourite. There was good music and there were burgers and everything like that. So, we hung out quite a lot," he recalled.Steyn also offered an interesting glimpse into Kohli's early days, describing him as a relatively laid-back youngster before commercial success and endorsements began changing his public image. While he recognised the Indian's natural ability, he felt the batter still needed some guidance at that stage of his career."In the early days of Virat Kohli, he was a normal T-shirt and shorts with the slops [flip-flops] kind of guy. Then the sponsors rolled in. You could tell, from a cricketing point of view, he was talented, but he needed a little bit of direction," Steyn added.Kohli's journey in the league, however, did not begin with such extraordinary numbers. Across his first three IPL seasons, Kohli accumulated 718 runs in 45 matches at an average of 21.75, registering just two half-centuries.He has since gone on to become the IPL's leading run-scorer, with 9,336 runs in 283 matches, including nine hundreds and 68 fifties. Between 2023 and 2026, he enjoyed another prolific phase, becoming the first batter in IPL history to register four consecutive seasons with more than 600 runs. Two of those campaigns also contributed to RCB's back-to-back title triumphs.At the international level, Kohli has crossed 28,000 runs and scored 86 centuries. He has also won all three major white-ball ICC titles - the ODI World Cup, T20 World Cup and Champions Trophy - besides collecting individual honours, including Player of the Tournament awards at World Cups in both formats and multiple Player of the Match awards in ICC events.Kohli's latest assignment was India's ODI series in New Zealand, where he scored 86 runs in four innings, including a half-century. He is expected to return to action against Sri Lanka in a three-match ODI series beginning December 13.In 14 ODIs and 13 innings this year, the former India captain has scored 638 runs at an average of 53.17 and a strike rate of over 118, with two centuries and four half-centuries.
Article Summary: Dale Steyn recalls his first impression of Virat Kohli during the 2008 Under-19 World Cup. The former South African fast bowler said Kohli struck him as a rather cocky youngster. However, their association at Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) brought the two closer.

Article Title: 'This 100 is for you!': Litton Das turns daughter's birthday into a special occasion with emotional celebration
Article Text:
Litton Das with his daughter Anayra. (Pic credit: Litton Das' FB post)

Litton, Hridoy script remarkable Bangladesh recovery

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Litton Das' special celebration after scoring hundred. (Pic credit: Litton Das' FB post)

Paterson leads South Africa's fightback

Litton Das gave his daughter Anayra a birthday present to cherish, celebrating her special day with a magnificent century against South Africa in the first Test at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. Unable to be with his little princess on her birthday, the Bangladesh batter found a special way to make the occasion memorable, dedicating his eighth Test hundred to her with a handwritten message that brought a personal touch to his fighting knock.After reaching the three-figure mark on the second morning, Das pulled out a handwritten note from his pocket and held it up for the cameras. The message read: "Happy Birthday to my Princess. This 100 is for you!"It was an emotional moment for the Bangladesh batter, who had already expressed his love for his daughter through a heartfelt social media post ahead of the occasion."Happy Birthday, my princess! I wish I could be with you on your special day, but even from afar, you are always in my thoughts and prayers. My blessings are with you, today and always. May you always be blessed with good health, happiness, and a beautiful heart. Grow up to be a wonderful person and keep shining, my little one. Your dad loves you more than words can ever express."The century was particularly special as Das had to overcome a difficult situation to put Bangladesh in a commanding position after their top order had collapsed on the opening day.Bangladesh were in deep trouble after opting to bat, with Kagiso Rabada ripping through their top order to reduce the visitors to 22/3 inside nine overs.The South African fast bowler dismissed debutant Mahfijul Islam, Mominul Haque and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto to put the hosts firmly in control.Towhid Hridoy and Tanzid Hasan then attempted to stabilise the innings with a 99-run partnership. Tanzid contributed 67 off 108 balls before Rabada struck again, removing him and Mushfiqur Rahim in quick succession. Bangladesh were 121/5 when Das joined Hridoy.What followed was a magnificent counterattack. The two batters stitched together a 206-run partnership for the sixth wicket, completely changing the complexion of the innings.Hridoy continued his impressive run in Test cricket, scoring 137 off 227 deliveries for his second century in just seven innings. He had struck a remarkable 224 against the West Indies recently.Das, meanwhile, brought up his half-century off 71 balls and finished the opening day unbeaten on 92. He needed only a few overs on Monday to complete his eighth Test century, becoming just the third Bangladesh batter to score a Test hundred against South Africa.He eventually departed for 120 off 179 balls, an innings featuring 14 fours and a six, after pulling Dane Paterson towards mid-wicket, where Marco Jansen completed the catch.Despite the resistance from Das and Hridoy, South Africa managed to bowl Bangladesh out for 400 before lunch on the second day.Paterson was the pick of the bowlers, claiming four wickets for 92 runs, while Rabada finished with five for 51. Jansen chipped in with two wickets.South Africa began their reply cautiously but suffered an early setback when Aiden Markram was caught behind off Hasan Mahmoud for four. The hosts were 18/1 at lunch.
Article Summary: Litton Das scores magnificent century against South Africa in first Test. Bangladesh batter dedicates his eighth Test hundred to his daughter Anayra. Das and Towhid Hridoy stitched together 206-run partnership for sixth wicket. South Africa bowled Bangladesh out for 400 before lunch on second day.

Article Title: Social media golf star Salim Sirur apologizes after 'drunken' Internet Invitational meltdown as Dave Portnoy delivers brutal verdict on 2027 return
Article Text:
Social media golf star Salim Sirur apologizes after 'drunken' Internet Invitational meltdown as Dave Portnoy delivers brutal verdict on 2027 return

Salim Sirur takes responsibility for drinking during Internet Invitational

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dave Portnoy rules out Salim Sirur’s return for 2027

Social media golf star Salim Sirur, also known as Salim The Dream, has apologised after his drunken behaviour during Dave Portnoy’s Internet Invitational golf tournament drew criticism. Sirur admitted that he put drinking ahead of his teammates and the match, saying he had let down Big John and Ryan Whitney. The influencer also shared an update on his recovery, revealing that he has not consumed alcohol since the tournament was filmed and is now 90 days sober. He accepted responsibility for his actions and said he regretted how he appeared in the episodes.Sirur represented Team Red alongside Big John and Ryan Whitney at Big Cedar Lodge in Missouri. During the fifth episode of Barstool Sports’ golf series, he was seen taking several shots of tequila. His drinking continued during the competition, and his behaviour became difficult for his teammates to handle.Following the backlash, Sirur addressed what happened in an apology video. He made it clear that he had failed to give his team the attention it deserved.‘I’m just going to get straight into it. I fed up,’ Sirur said.’I fed up big time. I prioritized drinking over focusing on the match and focusing with my teammates.‘I really want to apologize to Big John and Whitney, for me to just only think about drinking in that situation and not focus.’He also apologised to viewers who wanted to see a competitive finish.‘Also, I want to apologize to the fans. I know you guys expected a very competitive match in episode 6. And, like I said, I prioritized drinking over that.’The influencer then shared an important update about his decision to stop drinking. He explained that the tournament had been filmed months earlier and that August 13, 2026, was the last time he consumed alcohol.‘I had a huge problem back in the day. This was filmed three months ago, and I’m 90 days sober today. I haven’t drank since that last EP, which was August 13th, 2026.’Sirur also spoke about watching his own behaviour on screen. Although he initially found parts of Episodes 4 and 5 funny, he was unhappy with what he saw when he looked at the footage again.‘Taking a look back at it and really seeing how I was, I don’t like seeing myself that way. That wasn’t a good representation of myself.’He further said:‘I want to let everybody know too that I am doing really well,’ Sirur continued. ‘Obviously right now I have to relive this situation, and, you know, I deserve all of it. I deserve everything that’s coming to me. I deserve all the hate. I deserve all the comments.‘I deserve know, all- everything. I deserve everything. So if you guys want to give it to me, give it to me. I put myself in this position. I did it to myself, and, you know, I got to take accountability for it.’He thanked Barstool Sports for including him in the tournament and expressed hope that he would get another opportunity.‘I hope to get invited next year… something like this will never happen again.’However, Sirur’s hopes of returning may face a major obstacle. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy has already made his position clear about the influencer’s participation in the 2027 competition.‘Salim’s a nice kid and I hope he gets the help he needs,’ Portnoy said in a video. ‘But my god he fing ruined it the final match … It’s selfish to every motherfer there to do what he did. He will NOT be back next year. If he is, I’m OUT.’Portnoy’s comments make it clear that Sirur’s apology has not changed his decision. While Sirur wants another chance, his place in next year’s tournament is not something the Barstool founder is willing to support.
Article Summary: Social media golf star Salim Sirur has apologised after his drunken behaviour during Dave Portnoy’s Internet Invitational golf tournament. Sirur represented Team Red alongside Big John and Ryan Whitney at Big Cedar Lodge in Missouri. He accepted responsibility for his actions and said he regretted how he appeared in the episodes. The influencer also shared an update on his recovery, revealing that he has not consumed alcohol since the tournament was filmed and is now 90 days sober.

MUMBAI: Central Railway’s Mumbai Division will operate a megablock today to undertake essential engineering and maintenance works on its suburban network, affecting services on both the Main and Harbour lines.There will be no day block on Western Railway suburban section and this will be relief for those catching local trains today.On the Main Line, slow services between Thane and Kalyan will be blocked from 11am to 4pm.During the period, DOWN slow and semi-fast trains leaving Mulund between 10.43am and 3.53pm will be diverted to the fast corridor between Mulund and Kalyan, halting at Thane, Kalva, Mumbra, Diva and Dombivli stations.Similarly, UP slow and semi-fast services departing Kalyan between 10.36am and 3.51pm will run on the fast line up to Mulund before reverting to the slow corridor. Thane locals, however, will continue to operate on the designated slow line.On the Harbour Line, services between Panvel and Vashi will remain suspended from 11.05am to 4.05pm.Several Harbour and Trans-Harbour services between CSMT, Panvel and Thane will remain cancelled during the block period.CR chief spokesperson Swapnil Nila said that to minimise inconvenience, Central Railway will operate special local services between CSMT and Vashi, while services on the Port Line and between Thane-Vashi/Nerul will continue to run.

MUMBAI: Even as deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar called on chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday amid continuing speculation about the merger of the two NCP parties, working president of the NCP SP Supriya Sule categorically ruled out the possibility.She reiterated that this issue had reached a full stop the day her cousin, former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar , was killed in an air crash this Jan.“I am saying this for the final time. When my brother was alive, there were talks on a merger and a date had been fixed. The day he passed away -- in my mind and within our party -- there was a full-stop to this,” she said.She clarified that she had not received any proposal regarding the merger from the NCP. “I have not received any proposal by phone, WhatsApp, letter or any other means of communication,” she said.Responding to media questions on whether the NCP (SP) is considering joining the NDA alliance, she said, “There are no such talks. A full-stop can be spoken of only if talks are on.”Regarding her meetings with NCP leader Praful Patel in recent days, she said the two families have known each other for decades and that both of them were part of several parliamentary committees.“We meet regularly in the parliamentary committee on finance and FCRA. He was among the invitees for my daughter’s wedding,” said Sule.When asked about her response to Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Sanjay Raut ’s comment that talk of the merger was a myth and would fade in the next two days, she said, “He is like an elder brother to me and a senior leader in the MVA alliance. He has the right to say what he wants.”On the NCP (SP)’s possible support for the Centre’s delimitation bill, Sule said, “Six months ago, they had discussed this with several leaders of the INDIA bloc including me and Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Arvind Sawant. We felt that if the seats in all parliamentary constituencies uniformly rise by 50%, then there is no harm discussing this. The size of the electorate in each parliamentary constituency has risen from 13-14 lakh to 25-30 lakh and it is difficult for MPs to reach out to the entire constituency,” she saidHowever, she added, “There is no proposal before us at the moment. Nor have we seen the bill.”
Article Summary: Supriya Sule categorically ruled out the possibility of the merger of the two NCP parties. She reiterated that this issue had reached a full stop the day her cousin, former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar, was killed in an air crash this Jan.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay students call off 57-day sit-in, will continue dialogue with authorities
Article Text:
IIT Bombay students concluded their 57-day sit-in protest after recovering most of their confiscated belongings.

What Changed After 57 Days of Protest?

MUMBAI: After close to two months of agitation, IIT Bombay students have called off their sit-in protest following the return of belongings seized during a police intervention on campus last month. The decision came after talks with the Dean of Student Affairs and an email from institute director prof Shireesh Kedare outlining measures towards systemic reforms. It also coincides with the institute’s end semester exam which began on Nov 10.The protesting students, who had regrouped under Justice Corner 2.0, called it a victory for campus democracy. However, a laptop belonging to one student remains with the authorities, they claimed.The confrontation began on Sept 18 after the death by suicide of second year student Sahil Wakode.In an email to students on Friday, prof Kedare detailed initiatives undertaken over the semester, particularly the preceding two months, to address concerns raised by students and campus stakeholders.These included strengthening mental health support, reviewing hostel rules, improving grievance redressal mechanisms, expanding recreational facilities and upgrading campus infrastructure.Student representatives, faculty, alumni and administrators were working together on these initiatives, he said.“Meaningful institutional reform is a long-term effort,” Kedare wrote, stressing the need for patience, consistency and sustained engagement. He said the institute aimed to build systems that were more responsive to students, faculty and staff.The breakthrough followed a meeting with the Dean of Student Affairs. In a social media post, the Justice Corner collective said the administration had acknowledged several lapses in existing systems and assured students that their demands were being addressed.“We’ll hold them to it. Justice Corner will keep watch, follow up, and make sure every promise turns into action,” the collective said.The students, however, maintained that the return of their belongings was secured through collective pressure rather than administrative goodwill.“We are calling off our protest today; we have almost all of our confiscated belongings back. We received an email from the Director regarding our demands and future dialogue,” the collective announced, calling for a victory march at 9.30 pm on Friday.While the immediate standoff has ended, all eyes are on the police report and the findings of the enquiry committee set up by the IITB board of governors.The students have made clear that the protest’s withdrawal does not mean an end to their campaign. “We will continue fighting against every injustice,” they said.The 57-day student protest following Sahil Wakode’s death on September 18 has prompted several commitments and changes at IIT Bombay.On paper:- 18 demands: Director signed the students’ charter on September 20.- Mental health: 30 new counsellor posts announced.- Review committees: Panels constituted to examine the SC/ST Cell, hostel conditions and mental health concerns.- Examination rules: Revision underway to ensure students accused of violations can present their defence.On campus:- Student feedback: Regular surveys introduced to assess campus concerns.- Greater dialogue: Student bodies presenting reports at General Body Meetings; departmental open houses held or planned.- Communication: More direct administrative engagement on mental health, discrimination and student rights.- Everyday changes: Revised delivery timings and reportedly more responsive faculty and administrators.Still unresolved:- Release of the internal report on Sahil’s death.- Independent inquiry into the incident.- Safeguards for students facing disciplinary accusations.The sit-in has ended, but implementation remains the test.
Article Summary: The confrontation began on Sept 18 after the death by suicide of second year student Sahil Wakode. The decision came after talks with the Dean of Student Affairs and an email from institute director prof Shireesh Kedare outlining measures towards systemic reforms. However, a laptop belonging to one student remains with the authorities.

Article Title: Late drama in Bengaluru as Hannan salvages a point against Real Kashmir
Article Text:
In a thrilling Indian Football League match, FC Bengaluru United faced Real Kashmir FC at Bangalore

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





BENGALURU: There was late drama in the Indian Football League clash between FC Bengaluru United and Real Kashmir FC at the Bangalore Football Stadium here on Saturday. The visitors, leading 2-1, were sniffing victory, but Abdul Hannan had some other plans. The FCBU defender scored the all-important equaliser in the 90th minute.The Snow Leopards went close to scoring the winner in the six added minutes, but FCBU goalkeeper Manjunath Hirekurbar made a double save to salvage a point with a 2-2 draw for the home team.It was RKFC who looked in control during the initial exchanges. They used both the flanks effectively and made their possession count as forward Zahir Khan met Lalawmpuia Sailo’s cross to head into the empty net and take the lead in the 11th minute. However, FCBU regrouped after conceding the goal, and their efforts bore fruit ten minutes later.Colombian Maikol Andres Herrera fancied his chances from 25-odd yards. The long-ranger was out of the reach of Real Kashmir’s diving goalkeeper Susnata Malik to make it all square with a wonder strike into the top bin.It did not take long for the visitors to regain the lead with defender Shanid Valan scoring an outrageous goal.A miskick from midfielder Rohen Singh reached Valan inside the box, and he backheeled the ball above the goalkeeper to stun FCBU players in the 29th minute. Ribhav Sardesai then came close to making it all square, but his curling effort struck the crossbar.At the other end, FCBU defenders also made some last-minute tackles to keep the score 1-2 at the break. RKFC dominated possession for most of the second half, with FCBU being tactically outsmarted. Despite the dominance, they failed to find the net, though they came close with Amzard Khan striking the crossbar. But in the end, it was Hannan who emerged the hero as his late header helped FCBU snatch a draw.
Article Summary: FC Bengaluru United drew 2-2 with Real Kashmir FC at Bangalore Football Stadium. Abdul Hannan scored the all-important equaliser in the 90th minute. The Snow Leopards went close to scoring the winner in the six added minutes, but goalkeeper Manjunath Hirekurbar made a double save.

Article Text:

NEEMRANA: A Canadian woman travelled to Rajasthan hoping to marry a man she had befriended on a dating app. However, the man allegedly refused to marry her after meeting her in person, citing her age.Following a dispute between the two, the woman contacted the Canadian embassy, prompting police to intervene.The incident took place in Neemrana in Rajasthan's Behror district. Police reached the spot around 4am on November 13 after receiving information from the Canadian embassy. They took the woman and the man to the police station for questioning.According to Neemrana SHO Surendra Yadav, Nitin, a resident of Panipat in Haryana and son of Satyanarayan, had started communicating with the Canadian woman through a dating app around a year ago. Their friendship gradually developed into a relationship, and the two agreed to get married.The woman arrived in Delhi on November 11 on a tourist visa. Nitin went to the airport to receive her and brought her to a flat belonging to his maternal uncle and aunt in the BB Builders Society in Neemrana.The woman reportedly stayed with Nitin at the society for two days. However, when discussions about marriage progressed, Nitin allegedly backed out after learning that the woman was around 61 years old.This led to an argument between the two.On November 13, the woman contacted the Canadian embassy and informed officials about the developments. Following the embassy's communication, Neemrana police reached the society and took both of them to the police station.While police are questioning Nitin, the Canadian woman has been shifted to a care centre in Kotputli. Police are also making arrangements for her return to Canada.Nitin is reportedly employed as a teacher at a private school in Panipat. Further investigation into the matter is underway.
Article Summary: Canadian woman travelled to Rajasthan hoping to marry a man she had befriended on a dating app. However, the man allegedly refused to marry her after meeting her in person, citing her age. The woman contacted the Canadian embassy, prompting police to intervene.

Article Title: Delhi showroom murder: CCTV shows victim's final struggle with 'ex-friend' before killing

NEW DELHI: A CCTV footage from a clothing showroom in West Delhi's Moti Nagar has captured the final moments of an 18-year-old girl, showing her desperately trying to escape as a man allegedly assaults her before dragging her into a trial room and killing her.The footage reportedly shows the accused, identified as 29-year-old Suraj , repeatedly attacking Shabnam as she screams and attempts to flee. At one point, she sits down and tries to shield herself from the blows, but the man continues assaulting her.He is then seen dragging her by her hair into the trial room, where he allegedly slits her throat.Police arrested Suraj on Sunday and are questioning him to establish the exact motive behind Saturday's murder, including a suspected fallout following a romantic relationship, a police officer said.Shabnam worked at the showroom near Moti Nagar Metro Station. Her body was found inside the trial room by the staff later that evening, police said.According to the preliminary investigation, Shabnam and Suraj were on friendly terms, but their relationship had reportedly turned sour over the past few months. Police are also investigating allegations by the victim's family that the accused had assaulted her earlier.According to accounts shared by people familiar with the incident, Shabnam was seen using her mobile phone at the showroom around 6.45 pm on Saturday.Around 7.30pm, her employer could not locate her and contacted a woman who was Shabnam's former employer, informing her about the assault. The woman then reached the showroom.Some people examined the CCTV footage and noticed that the man had left the premises, but Shabnam had not."Suspecting that she could still be inside, they returned to the showroom around 8.30pm and began searching the premises. During the search, they noticed her scarf lying near the trial room. They also spotted blood seeping out from underneath the door," the officer said.Her body was found around 9pm, following which the police were called.A police team that reached the spot found injury marks on her neck caused by a sharp-edged weapon, along with a blood-stained knife near her body. The body was sent to Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital for a post-mortem.Police examined CCTV footage from inside the showroom and nearby areas to piece together the sequence of events, establish the accused's movements and trace his escape route.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows 18-year-old girl desperately trying to escape as a man allegedly assaults her. He is then seen dragging her by her hair into the trial room, where he allegedly slits her throat. Police arrested Suraj on Sunday and are questioning him to establish the exact motive.

VARANASI: A 2023-batch police sub-inspector, Sandeep Kumar , 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district.Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him.Ballia SP Iraj Raja on Sunday said that following collection of evidences and lodging of a complaint by Kumar's wife the accused woman Roli Gond was arrested from an orchard near the railway station on the charges of abetment of suicide.Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.Earlier, the incident came to light when a train’s loco pilot informed the Chitbaragaon station master through a memo that someone had jumped before his moving train to commit suicide.On being alerted by railway officials Chitbadagaon police and GRP reached the spot, where Kumar's motorbike and mobile phone were found lying near the railway track while his mutilated body was detected on tracks.On getting information Raja, ASP South Sanjay Verma, CO Akshay Kumar and railway police officials also reached there while forensic team was engaged to collect evidence from the railway track area.Kumar, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar, was married and had a six-month-old child. He had been posted at Chitbaragaon police station for past 11 months.He was transferred to Pakri police station but had not yet been relieved from his old posting because of Chhath festival arrangements. On Saturday evening, he had left police station by informing colleagues that he was going to his duty point.After postmortem examination the mortal remain of Kumar was brought to the police lines, where following guard of honours officials paid tributes and observed silence for two minutes.The officials also consoled Kumar's family, which also remained at police lines.
Article Summary: Sandeep Kumar, 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district. Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him. Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.

Article Title: Another setback for AAP in Punjab: Sukhdeep Singh Chhina resigns from posts, primary membership
Article Text:
Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, who served as the Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, has officially stepped down from all roles within the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)

AAP faces a series of exits in Punjab





CHANDIGARH: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has suffered another exit in Punjab , with Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, resigning from all party positions and the party's primary membership.Chhina submitted his resignation to AAP Punjab president Aman Arora, formally announcing his decision to sever ties with the party.In his resignation letter addressed to Arora, Chhina wrote: "I, Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, hereby tender my resignation from all positions held in the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and also relinquish my primary membership of the party."The letter does not specify a reason for his decision. Chhina has announced his resignation from party positions and primary membership; the statement provided does not mention whether he is also stepping down as Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board.Chhina's resignation comes amid a series of departures from the AAP in Punjab. Earlier this month, two party MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, resigned from the party's primary membership, a day after AAP announced its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.The two resignations came as the party began preparations for the next Assembly polls. AAP has also faced political criticism and dissent from within its Punjab unit in recent weeks.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, who served as the Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, has officially stepped down from all roles within the Aam Aadmi Party. His resignation comes amid a series of departures from the AAP in Punjab. Earlier this month, two party MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra resigned from the party's primary membership.
